Both tag-filtering options work. They're identical except for how you pick the tag to filter by. In each, you have the tag *reading* on two of the three example bookmarks.

**Version A — a filter bar of your tags**
→ http://maker:4001/filter-a.html

Try this: above the list you'll see a row of your tags. **Click "reading."** The list narrows to the 2 bookmarks tagged *reading*, the chip highlights, and the count shows "showing 2 of 3." Click **"All"** to clear.

**Version B — click a tag right on a bookmark**
→ http://maker:4001/filter-b.html

Try this: on any bookmark card, **click its "reading" tag.** The list narrows the same way, and a banner appears at the top ("Showing only tag: reading") with a **✕ clear** to remove it.

Both filter to one tag at a time and both still work alongside the search box.

One choice I made in both, so it's visible: **picking a tag filters to that one tag (not adding several tags together).** Tell me if one-at-a-time is fine or if you'd expect to stack multiple tags.

Try each and tell me **which way of filtering feels more natural** — then we'll do the sort order.
